evidence: The changelog said the ERR trap routes the `SELF=` assembly into `_refuse`, but `SELF="$(cd ... && pwd)/$(basename ...)"` reports the status of the last substitution only. The agent's own test showed `status=0 SELF='/finalize-session'`. The agent fixed both the code (the SELFDIR split) and the text instead of only softening the claim.
guidance_note: When a changelog or comment says a new mechanism covers specific named lines, run a failing case through each named line before writing the claim, especially an assignment that contains more than one command substitution.

evidence: The file's own `_process_identity` already treats a `ps -p` that exits 0 with empty output as a failure, and the new `CLAUDE_CMD=$(ps ...) || _refuse` checked only the exit status. Instead of the reviewer's inline `[ -n ]` at each call site, the agent extracted a `_process_command` helper shaped like `_process_identity`. Both transports call it, and two fixture tests cover it.
guidance_note: When adding a new read of an idiom the file already wraps with an invariant (here `ps -p` plus an empty-output check), reuse or mirror that wrapper instead of writing a fresh inline read.

evidence: The hunk shows the original `2>/dev/null` dropped from the extracted `ps` read, so `ps`'s raw diagnostic would print next to the `_refuse` message. The agent conceded it had misapplied no-silent-failure, and its reply states the law correctly: nothing is swallowed when the code refuses loudly in its own voice.
guidance_note: Before removing a stderr redirect in the name of no-silent-failure, check whether the failure is still reported by name. If it is, the redirect only removes a duplicate message and should stay.

evidence: This is the same defect as F1, in the code comment. The agent reproduced it (`assignment status=0 SELF='/finalize-session'`), split the assignment so the `cd` failure reaches `_refuse`, rewrote the comment to say where the trap's reach ends, and grepped for other concatenated assignments.
guidance_note: When introducing an ERR trap as a catch-all, list the failure shapes it cannot see (assignments that mask a failure, condition contexts) and grep for them in the same commit.

narrative: All four findings came in round 0 against the original PR. Two of them (F1 and F4) are one defect: the ERR trap was claimed to cover a concatenated `SELF=` assignment that cannot fail visibly. F2 and F3 came from the agent's own extraction of the `ps` read: it did not apply the file's empty-output invariant and it dropped the stderr redirect. One fix commit resolved all four, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent wrote coverage claims into a release-notes changelog and a code comment without testing each line those claims named. The fix-time tests it then wrote showed the claim was false in one command.
The fix replies are strong: they reproduce the bug before fixing it, sweep for the same shape, and correct a misapplied law instead of defending it.

evidence: Only `FINISHING.mark` is read (`FINISHING.mark in turn_opening(...)`), so `CLOSING.mark` was dead data that duplicated a phrase in CLOSING.reason. Commit 9be6030 removes the field and splices a single `FINISHING_MARK` constant into FINISHING.reason, so the matched phrase and the shown phrase cannot drift. This is more than the reviewer's suggestion of dropping the field and narrowing the comment.
guidance_note: When adding a namedtuple field to support a lookup, check that every instance's value is actually read; a field filled for symmetry alone is dead data.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. bbe38df only changed `text_of`/`turn_opening` content reading. The single `"spent"` label for both bands is in the original PR's change to `stop()`, shown in this finding's hunk. The premise holds: one label covered both a harmless continuation under the grace and a spent forced close-out that 'starts with nothing'. Commit 9be6030 logs `spent-{band.label}`, with tests for both labels.
guidance_note: When splitting one outcome into banded variants, carry the band into every logged label the old single outcome emitted, not only into the message text.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. bbe38df did not touch the band reasons. The asymmetry is in the original PR text: FINISHING ends 'Do not move the ceiling to make room' and CLOSING ends 'Do not start new work'. The hard-limit band was the one missing the prohibition, and 9be6030 adds it to CLOSING.
guidance_note: When a new prohibition is added to one of two parallel messages, decide for each sibling whether it applies there too; for a prohibition both need, put it in the shared CLOSE_OUT suffix instead of a per-band clause.

evidence: The named fix commit 9be6030 added the 'do not move the ceiling' clause to CLOSING and added test assertions only for the spent labels (F2). Nothing pinned the clause in either band. e2c5355 then added `"move the ceiling" in out["reason"]` checks for both bands.
guidance_note: When a fix restores text that a review found missing from one place, add the test that would have caught the omission in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. e2c5355 only added two test assertions, and the stale SKILL.md numbers come from the original PR's `DEFAULT_CEILING = 350_000` bump (shown in the hunk). The packet does not include SKILL.md, but the reviewer and the agent describe the same worked example (250,000 + 100,000 = 350,000), and the agent updated it to 450,000 in 6aeb7aa.
guidance_note: When changing a default constant, grep the docs and skills for worked examples that compute from the old value, not just for the literal old value.

narrative: Two of the seven rounds (0 and 2) were cancelled runs and posted nothing. Most findings were in the original PR's text and were found late: F2 and F3 in round 3, and F5 (stale SKILL.md numbers from the default bump) only in round 5. Their post-review flags are false positives, because the flagged commits touched unrelated code. The one fix-caused finding is F4: 9be6030 added the CLOSING ceiling-raise clause without a test, which cost round 4.
guidance_observations: Bumping a default constant should come with a docs sweep for derived numbers. The stale SKILL.md example went unnoticed until the fifth review run and cost its own round.

Fix commits added tests for some fixes (the spent labels) but not others (the prohibition clause) in the same commit. Applying one rule to every behavior a fix commit changes would have removed a round.
